text.insert: Resolved design questions with their decisions, moved out of Open questions. Each section keeps the original question context, its decision callout, and any later amendment beneath it.
Learning writer contract
Workers must emit learnings (and verdicts on learnings they relied on) as part of the attempt record — a prompt-contract change.
What's the minimum viable shape that doesn't burden the matching loop?
Learnings ride the final worker report: the existing end-of-run summary schema gains optional
learnings[]
and
learning_verdicts[]
arrays, validated at the ship gate. No mid-loop tool call or extra prompt surface — understanding is captured once, at the moment the worker already writes its summary.

props.title: Amendment (2026-08-10) — inference moves to the librarian

text.insert: Superseding the original contract entirely: the worker authors no report. The librarian condenses the run transcript and state directly — attempts into the attempt ledger, learnings into the knowledge ledger. Nothing depends on a worker summarization step; transcript completeness is the fidelity ceiling, and transcripts are complete by construction.
Corroboration threshold
How many independent confirmations (or one strong evidence type, e.g. an upstream rename) before
proposed → corroborated
Who/what adjudicates — the curator job?
proposed
corroborated

on two independent worker confirmations, OR one strong evidence type alone (upstream rename, merged naming PR, or an exact-match attempt that relied on the learning). The curator job adjudicates mechanically on its existing cadence — no new adjudicator.
Graduation pipeline
Who drafts upstream naming/comment PRs from corroborated learnings — a dedicated agent lane, or bundled into match PRs?
Bundled into match PRs: when a slice PR touches a function with a corroborated
name_proposal

, the rename/comment rides along — the match is the proof, consistent with the ribbanya cross-module ruling. No dedicated graduation lane for now; revisit if corroborated learnings pile up on functions no match PR will touch.
Graduation is deferred entirely — see “graduation deferred, names stay internal” below. The match-PR mechanism remains the plan for when graduation turns on.
CALLS edge source
Clang AST pass vs. ctags-level heuristics vs. map/objdiff data.
Is "VS Code-grade" required, or are ~90%-accurate heuristic edges enough for injection ranking?

Heuristic first, clang later. Ship ctags/regex-grade extraction over the checkout now — ~90%-accurate edges are enough for injection ranking, where a missed edge costs one hint, not correctness. Keep the builder's edge shape stable so a clang AST pass can replace the extractor later without a schema change.
The extractor is neither ctags-grade heuristics nor clang:
build/GALE01/asm/
carries fully symbolized call sites (binary-side ground truth), so CALLS/DATA_REFS derive from the disassembly joined to source via
report.json
. The clang fallback is unnecessary. See the lane-1 decision below.
Symptom vocabulary
Start with the ten mismatch categories as controlled vocabulary; let signatures (section, instruction class, diff shape) grow under them.
How structured does the trigger need to be before it beats text search over objdiff output?

Category plus free-text signature. The controlled vocabulary is exactly the ten mismatch-pattern categories; under each, signatures (section, instruction class, diff shape) stay free text matched by search. Structure only where it's stable — recurring signature clusters can be promoted to sub-categories later from ledger evidence.
Negative results
"Tactic tried, didn't work" requires workers to self-report tactics — same prompt-contract change as learnings.
Worth it from day one?
Yes, from day one — and graded, not boolean. Every tactic tried is filed by the librarian from the run transcript alongside learnings, with a graded outcome instead of
worked: true|false
failed
(no score movement),
partial
(score moved toward 100% but not exact),
success
(reached 100% / exact). Tactic applications are ordered by timestamp within the attempt, and failures are always recorded so efficacy ranking has real denominators.
Sibling extraction
Naming-convention rules (character prefixes, move suffixes) are mechanical but Melee-specific.
Where do they live — game config or builder code?
Game config. The naming-convention rules (character prefixes, move suffixes) live as data under
games/melee/
; a generic
builders/siblings.ts
interprets them. Builder code stays game-agnostic, consistent with how the harness already separates game knowledge (tree guide, crosswalk) from engine code.
Crosswalk scope
Today it covers
ft
chars.
Extend the same mechanical treatment to stages/items (
gr*
it*
→ stage/item pages)?
Extend now: add
gr*
→ stage pages and
it*
→ item pages alongside the existing
ft
character coverage. Same mechanical table format, two more prefix families; the wiki mirror already holds those pages. No
if
mn
lb
sweep — those areas have weak or no wiki counterparts.
Boot digest budget
How much of each per-target attachment gets injected at boot — ranking and size caps for the 1-hop digest, attempt digest, and knowledge digest?
What wins when a target is knowledge-rich but token budget is tight?

The boot object is minimal: a top-level card — here's the target, here's its record (scores, claim state, shorthand pointers into its attachments). It is shorthand for quick lookup; the agent walks the graph for everything else. No bulk digest injection at boot.
Epoch rebuild trigger
The code graph and search indexes rebuild "each epoch" — is the trigger the epoch boundary, a master merge, or both?
Is a mid-epoch rebuild ever needed (e.g. after a big merge-update)?

Knowledge maintenance already runs on three cadences — every 5 minutes when idle, a fast pass every 3 minutes or 16 new reports, and a full pass at each epoch boundary. The question reduces to which cadence rebuilds which layer.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-10) — incremental per worker, full per epoch

text.insert: No mid-epoch full builds. As each worker finishes, knowledge maintenance runs incrementally and updates the agent-facing knowledge graph. The full computed builds — Ghidra, opseq, and the other search indexes — run at epoch boundaries, epoch by epoch.
Discord backlog strategy
Forward-only daily cron, or a one-time historical backfill first?
Channel scope — all channels or a curated subset?

The semantics changed enough that most of the knowledge base gets rebuilt from scratch: all of Discord, all past PRs, and the worker logs are reprocessed through the librarian intake. The per-source rebuild processes get detailed in the migration map.
Knowledge ledger physical format
JSONL under
games/melee/knowledge/
vs a DB table — which, and where exactly?
The curator write path exists (
appendCuratedKnowledgeRecords
pattern); does the ledger reuse that file layout or get its own?
The curator already appends to
knowledge_curator_updates.jsonl
— extending that JSONL family is the path of least resistance.
Lean: a JSONL-family store, extending the curator's existing
knowledge_curator_updates.jsonl
pattern. The open part is searchability — whether JSONL plus an index (the graph DB or SQLite) is enough for direct search, or the ledger needs a different queryable store.

Searchability decides the format: the ledger uses whatever store gives the best search across the whole knowledge base. JSONL is acceptable as the append log only with a real search index over it (SQLite FTS or the graph DB); if a different queryable store searches better, it wins. Good search across everything is the requirement — storage format is subordinate.
Corroboration numbers per origin
Exact confidence priors for
human_extracted
vs
ai_inferred
, and whether a human statement + one AI confirm counts as corroborated.

Promotion is consistency-based, not a fixed count: most learnings are naming and code↔game links that upstream reviewers cannot validate, so corroboration is internal — the system runs, and consistent independent findings ('maybe this links to X' recurring across attempts and doors) raise confidence until promotion. Exact thresholds stay open.

No fixed numbers. The librarian corroborates by judgment at intake: when the details of new material consistently confirm an existing learning, it marks it corroborated. Consistency over count, per the earlier direction — thresholds can be formalized later if judgment proves noisy.
Graduation readiness
What exactly marks a corroborated
name_proposal
as PR-ready, and who drafts the rename/comment text inside the match PR?

props.title: Decision (2026-08-10) — graduation deferred, names stay internal

text.insert: No name proposals graduate right now. Names live in the internal knowledge base as “this is what we think it is” — they never make it into a PR at this stage. Graduation to upstream renames is revisited once the ledger has proven itself.
Transcript economics
The transcript linkage is broken today —
pi_sessions.session_file
points at pre-migration paths; the worker door needs it repaired first.
Retention: transcripts total ~1.3 GB and grow per run — how long do we keep them once condensed?
Condensation depth: timeline-first (~4 KB
activity.jsonl
+ checkpoints) with transcript escalation on demand, or always full-transcript (~1 MB per worker)?

props.title: Decision (2026-08-10) — condense, keep for analysis, prune later

text.insert: Keep full transcripts for now — they are not a meaningful amount of disk and they are useful for analysis. Once a transcript has been condensed into the system, the full text is no longer needed and can be removed later. The
pi_sessions
linkage repair still has to happen for condensation to read them.
Checkpoint as attempt substrate
Adopt
worker_checkpoints
as the source of truth for observed attempts, with the attempt record as a derived view (checkpoint + librarian tactic overlay)?
If yes, the attempt ledger needs no new capture path for worker runs — only the transform and the overlay.
worker_checkpoints

is the source of truth for observed attempts; the attempt record is a derived view over it plus the librarian's tactic overlay. The librarian does less — it files and overlays rather than reconstructing.
Per-epoch index builds (lane 1)
Lane 1 — per-epoch index builds
The template already exists.
opseq is the pattern to copy: an extractor (
toolpacks/.../opseq/runners/extract_opcode_sequences.py
) reads the build outputs and writes JSONL indexes under
games/melee/shared/tool-data/
; a graph builder reads those and emits edges plus per-target facts. Every new index follows this shape.
CALLS / DATA_REFS — proposal: derive from the disassembly, not source parsing.
build/GALE01/asm/
already contains 80,510 fully symbolized
bl <symbol>
call sites across 20,959 function boundaries — binary-side ground truth. Parse per-function branch targets, join to source via
report.json
(the same join opseq uses). No ctags, no clang, no new tooling — the original heuristic-vs-clang question dissolves.
Ghidra — proposal: add the xref export.
The toolpack is already live (analyzed project on disk,
symbol_lookup.jsonl
and
function_shapes.jsonl
exports exist); xrefs are a declared capability with no export yet. Adding xref cache rows gives a second, independent call/data-ref source to cross-check the asm-derived edges.
Siblings — proposal: bootstrap the config from existing prose.
No machine-readable prefix table exists — the rules live in tree-guide Markdown (34 character pages,
ftKirby → ftKb
table) and the crosswalk's 117 glob rows. One-time distillation into the game-config rule table under
games/melee/
, then the generic builder consumes it per the earlier decision.
Staleness fix comes free.
Current opseq indexes are dated and their evidence refs point into a dead cycle tree — exactly the drift the per-epoch rebuild decision eliminates once these builds run at epoch boundaries.

All lane-1 proposals approved: CALLS/DATA_REFS derived from the disassembly's symbolized call sites; the Ghidra xref export built out (the toolpack is half-baked today — building it out is the work); the sibling rule table bootstrapped from tree-guide and crosswalk prose. Every index standardizes on the opseq template — extractor → JSONL under
shared/tool-data/
→ graph builder → edges and per-target facts — rebuilt at epoch boundaries. More data and better standardization is the improvement axis.

Backfill does not replay history as a naive reader. Every extracted statement anchors against the current checkout first (content hash · symbol existence): anchors hold → live proposed learning; anchor fails → historical note or drop. Chronology enters as timestamps on evidence, which resolve supersession — later statements win, contradicted ones are refuted on arrival with their evidence kept. The journey of how understanding changed survives in the evidence chains, not in processing order.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-10) — Discord repull, one door two ranges

text.insert: Discord gets re-pulled raw with timestamps via a Discord CLI exporter, replacing the distilled markdown as source of truth (the markdown remains a cross-check corpus). The exporter is the pipeline: backfill = run from the beginning, the daily cron = run since yesterday. One door, two ranges.
There is exactly one knowledge kernel agent: the librarian. The separate knowledge-curator and pr-indexer agents are retired; the librarian carries their duties as doors —
condense
curation
pr_indexing

— one role, one schema (librarian_v1 with optional door sections). Deterministic extraction and graph builders stay plain code. Kernel catalog went 10 → 8 agents; legacy CLI flags and output contracts kept for compatibility. Implemented same day.
Every item in a librarian batch carries an explicit
kind

(checkpoint, transcript span, PR, discord message, …) in the input — the agent never infers item type. The prompt gives per-kind handling rules; multi-kind guidance applies only to genuinely mixed batches.
The librarian searches everything relevant: code graph, past PRs, the smashwiki corpus, and — critically —
ledger_search

over its own knowledge ledger, without which corroboration-by-judgment cannot check new statements against existing learnings. All doors advertise the full tool set; the condense door's byte-compat freeze is lifted after Ford's review.
Resolved by execution (2026-08-11)

The completed run replaced the remaining per-source backfill questions with executed contracts: past PRs completed 1,168 manifest batches; checkpoint-grounded worker history completed 836 target-group batches covering the 3,460 of 3,987 workers with checkpoints; and Discord completed its available synced-month range as one batch. The landed raw puller defines discord-cli as the primary engine and the direct API as fallback. All 2,005 planned batches finished, manifest retries recovered transient failures, and corroboration operated as a separate resumable pass.
History

Deliverable-1 fan-out landed (prune, per-target indexes, ledger, librarian, backfill driver, discord puller); librarian consolidated to one knowledge agent with three doors and the full tool surface; full backfill executed (2,005 batches, jobs ramp settled at 64); corroboration pass, HAS_LEARNING graph builder, and the /knowledge dashboard tab shipped; as-built docs moved to the knowledge section.

2026-08-10 — v11: open questions pruned to the nine genuinely open items; the eight resolved round-1 questions and their decisions moved to the new decision log.

learnings[]
learning_verdicts[]
, edge
HAS_LEARNING
, state-shape LearningRecord); connection-map canvas labels updated to match.

subject: symbol | file | area | general
, smashwiki corpus, standards), inputs slimmed to past PRs · discord · retired; design chapters folded into the sections they describe.
